question: Does a domino-torus crystal that becomes collar-legal only after three cuts admit the last one-bit decoration of the pinwheel, s(0) = 10101, s(1) = 00110: a periodic labelling of one of its cuts obeying the decoration's labelled collar law?

public_inputs.planes: The 96,416 domino tilings of the 2 x 2 to 4 x 4 tori with every diagonal choice (PINWHEEL-ATLAS-20261107-001B's family F3), with collars computed exactly as in ONE-BIT-20261108-001B's run.py (imported unchanged).
public_inputs.classes: A collar type is of class 1 if it lies in the level-one law of COLLAR-PLANE-20261108-001B (level_one_law.json), class 2 if all five children's collars (one geometric cut) are of class 1, class 3 if all five children's collars are of class 1 or 2, and 0 otherwise. A plane is legal after j cuts when all its collar types have class between 1 and j; it is kept when j = 3 and its multiset of collar types is new.
public_inputs.decoration: s(0) = 10101, s(1) = 00110, its law by ROUND-PRICE-20261108-001A's decor_lib; its relabelling has the same verdicts (ROUND-PRICE-20261108-001A's control).
public_inputs.test: For each kept plane, the k-fold cut for k = 3, 4, 5 is admitted when a periodic labelling on a torus of index 1 or 2 over the plane's lattice obeys the law (decor_lib.periodic); the search stops at the first admitted k.

forbidden_inputs: Changing the family, the classes, the decoration, the levels or the tori after seeing results
primary_observable: Whether some kept plane admits the decoration, with its first admitted level.
secondary_observables: The numbers of collar types of each class and of planes legal after three cuts, by torus.
cheapest_meaningful_control: Positive: the classes agree with ONE-BIT-20261108-001B's filter on classes 1 and 2 (the same 32 and 176 planes legal within one and two cuts); the decoration 10001 / 01100 is admitted by ONE-BIT-20261108-001B's mixed 4 x 4 plane after three cuts (it was admitted there after two), so the labelled test can say yes. Negative: the plain rectangle lattice gets class 0. A run whose controls fail is not read.
first_executable_signal: The class counts and the controls.
decision_or_followup_rule: If a kept plane admits the decoration, it fails: one bit per tile, as a decorated substitution, fails in every case. If none does, the decoration stays open with this family and these levels as its tested range.
stop_rule: Stop at the declared family, classes, decoration, levels and tori.
nonclaims: Exploratory and non-promotable: one family of periodic planes and three levels.
No kept plane admitting the decoration does not show that it forces the pinwheel.
feasibility_disclosure: Before freezing: no run of this search. ONE-BIT-20261108-001B's filter (the same planes, classes 1 and 2) took about ten minutes on 16 workers and kept 11 distinct planes, none of which admits this decoration within two levels past its first legal cut.
